arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Schein's lawyer argued the FAA mandates enforcing delegation clauses.
Archer's lawyer argued the FAA's plain language contradicts Schein's view.
Justice Sotomayor questioned the lack of statutory remedies for groundless claims.
Justice Ginsburg questioned how Schein claims benefits from an agreement it did not make.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on who decides if a contract is valid enough to force arbitration. Schein wants arbitrators to decide this. Archer wants courts to decide it first.

paragraphs: This case defines the power of arbitrators versus courts. It determines who decides if a contract is valid. It affects every business with an arbitration clause. It shapes the balance of power in commercial disputes.
